subject: E1B9B332AC67E6035B1C4BC3B01EA8BB
introduction: The Kitáb-i-Aqdas asks each believer to wash, sit, turn to God and repeat “Alláh-u-Abhá”, God is Most Glorious, ninety-five times each day; these readings give the law, its roots in the Báb’s writings, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s encouragement to say the Greatest Name on waking, in trouble and at work. Remembrance by repetition of a divine Name is one of the most widespread devotions there is: the Qur’an’s “remember Allah with much remembrance” and “in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest”, the Psalmist’s “seven times a day”, Paul’s “pray without ceasing”. Jesus’s warning against “vain repetitions” is the caution every such practice has to answer.
questions: What is the difference between repeating a Name ninety-five times and the “much speaking” Jesus warns against?
Reading 2 suggests the Name for moments of trouble and of work. How does a fixed daily practice relate to that spontaneous use?
Why might a religion with almost no ritual keep this one?

outside.why: The Qur’an’s command behind every such practice in Islam and after it: O ye who believe! Remember Allah with much remembrance.
Each day, having washed, to repeat “Alláh-u-Abhá” ninety-five times. Seven times a day do I praise thee because of thy righteous judgments.

Jesus warned against a kind of repetition: use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking. What makes a repeated Name of God something other than that?
In trouble, under opposition, at work, say the Name. The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
From the sun’s rising to its setting. Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray.
“The Greatest Name should be read every day.” Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks.
One who would divide the friends begins by seeming devoted to a verse. Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep’s clothing.
Recite the Greatest Name every morning. My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O Lord.
Continue in that rejoicing. Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!
A meeting opened by saying the Name in silence. The Lord is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him.
The blessed Name alone as greeting. A name which is above every name.
